Across 50-round traces, TokenTrap amplifies token consumption by $2{,}487.0\times$, $1{,}616.0\times$, and $567.8\times$ relative to a no-token-task baseline for the three workflows. Its router achieves 85.67% accuracy on 300 architecture-labeled prompts. These results demonstrate that short, non-sensitive requests can impose substantial context-processing and coordination costs, motivating resource-aware defense as a complement to scam detection.

Die Debatte um eine „zeitgemäße Prüfungskultur“ unter Bedingungen generativer Künstlicher Intelligenz verschärft ein Grundproblem schulischer Leistungsbewertung: Aus einem vorliegenden Produkt ist nicht mehr zuverlässig auf die eigenständigen kognitiven Operationen seines vermeintlichen Urhebers zu schließen. Während Dänemark häuslich erstellte Abschlussarbeiten durch mündliche Prüfungen ergänzen will und in Australien die University of Sydney beaufsichtigte und offene Prüfungsformen systematisch trennt, institutionalisiert Nordrhein-Westfalen ab dem Abiturjahrgang 2030 ein fünftes, den anderen vier Fächern gleichwertig gewichtetes Abiturprüfungsfach mit Präsentationsprüfung und reflexivem Fachgespräch. Parallel verändern ab 2027 novellierte Kernlehrpläne die Unterrichts- und Leistungsanforderungen. Das vorliegende Working Paper prüft die Tragfähigkeit dieser Antworten anhand eines argumentationsbasierten Validitätsverständnisses. Seine zentrale These lautet: Die nachträgliche Reflexion einer KI-gestützt vorbereiteten Leistung kann gegenwärtiges Können zeigen; sie authentifiziert jedoch nicht den vorausgegangenen Entstehungsprozess. ENGLISH The debate over what constitutes a “contemporary assessment culture” in the age of generative artificial intelligence raises a fundamental question about educational assessment: To what extent can the quality of a submitted piece of work still serve as reliable evidence of the independent cognitive effort of the person claiming authorship? While Denmark is planning to supplement take-home final assignments with oral examinations, the University of Sydney in Australia has introduced a systematic distinction between supervised and open assessment formats. Meanwhile, the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia is introducing a fifth examination subject for the 2030 Abitur, carrying the same weight as the other four subjects and assessed through a presentation followed by an oral discussion. Revised subject curricula, taking effect from 2027, will also reshape teaching and assessment requirements. Drawing on an argument-based approach to assessment validity, this working paper critically examines whether these responses can support the claims made about individual student achievement. Its central argument is that reflecting retrospectively on work prepared with AI assistance may demonstrate what a student currently knows and understands, but it cannot establish who performed the cognitive work involved in producing the original submission.

This study explores the foundations of language-learning motivation based on self-determination theory. It distinguishes between intrinsic and extrinsic motivational factors and amotivation, while examining global, contextual, and situational levels of motivation. Extrinsic goals are considered along the continuum of their internalization by learners, ranging from external regulation to integrated regulation. Particular attention is paid to the personal significance of language learning, which may coexist with enjoyment of the learning process itself. The study also examines criteria for success, including mastery-oriented and performance-oriented approaches. Conditions for learner engagement are described in terms of the satisfaction of the needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness. The research considers Pearson correlation coefficient data concerning the relationship between intrinsic motivation and positive attitudes toward learning English. Questionnaires, interviews, and qualitative analysis of learners’ statements are employed to investigate motivation. These methods help preserve the meaning of individual responses and distinguish between learners’ stated goals, specific learning experiences, and self-assessments of their own progress.

Introduction: Healthcare systems are increasingly complex and variable in the digital era. Nurses must process large volumes of information and make clinical decisions under time constraints, which increases their cognitive load, while conventional nursing documentation offers limited insight into clinical reasoning and learning from actual practice. Objective: To synthesize knowledge on Focus Charting and explain the role of its Focus–Data–Action–Response (F-DAR) structure in reducing cognitive load, supporting clinical reasoning, promoting proactive patient safety in line with Safety-II, and enabling artificial intelligence (AI) applications in digital health systems. Methods: A narrative review was conducted using a systematic literature search of CINAHL, PubMed, Scopus, ThaiJO, and Google Scholar between March 2025 and March 2026. Thai- and English-language publications from 2000 to 2025 were eligible. Of the 198 records identified, 65 were included and analyzed using content analysis combined with conceptual synthesis. Results and Conclusion: Five key themes emerged: (1) the nursing process provides the professional logic underpinning meaningful documentation; (2) the F-DAR structure functions as a condensed nursing process that systematically links data, decisions, interventions, and outcomes, and has the potential to reduce redundancy and cognitive load while supporting clinical reasoning; (3) compared with narrative and SOAP formats, F-DAR is distinguished by its explicit documentation of patient responses; (4) the Response component captures work-as-done and nurses’ adaptations, thereby facilitating learning consistent with Safety-II; and (5) well-structured F-DAR data provide a foundation for health information systems and AI applications in nursing, provided that data governance and nurse oversight are maintained. Direct empirical evidence of the effect of F-DAR on cognitive loads is limited. Focus Charting has the potential to reduce cognitive load, support clinical reasoning, promote Safety-II learning, and provide a foundation for digital nursing innovations. Experimental studies are required to confirm its effectiveness in the Thai healthcare context.

This study investigates the influence of spirituality on the management of work-life integration among healthcare professionals, highlighting a comprehensive amalgamation of personal, professional, and emotional aspects.In the demanding healthcare environment, professionals often face stress, emotional fatigue, and ethical dilemmas that impact their health and performance.The study examines the influence of spiritual orientation, as manifested through mindfulness, compassion, purpose, and inner balance, on individuals' ability to reconcile their professional and personal lives.An examination of essential aspects of spirituality, such as spiritual resilience, integration, compassion, and spiritual sensitivity, is conducted to comprehend their impact on work-life integration.The results show that spirituality is an important mental resource that helps people be more emotionally resilient, make better moral choices, and be happier with their lives in general.Moreover, the findings indicate that promoting spirituality within healthcare organizations can enhance employee well-being, fortify organizational culture, and elevate the quality of patient care.This study adds to the growing conversation about how to include spirituality in human resource management and occupational health practices in the healthcare field.

In this paper, we present 5uGUE, a large language model (LLM)-driven hardware-in-the-loop agent, which enables the wireless fuzzing of 5G-enabled devices (such as mobile phones). 5uGUE combines multi-step reasoning with tool-assisted interaction and integrates into the fuzzing pipeline by leveraging specialized tools for internet search, 5G protocol analysis, memory management, and test-case execution. The agent iteratively generates test cases, executes them on targets, collects runtime feedback, and adaptively refines the fuzzing strategy. We evaluate 5uGUE on five commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) 5G devices across six LLMs. The best performing runs for 5uGUE trigger 167 crashes in total (141 novel and 31 unique) within 60 interaction turns (49 to 133 minutes total runtime). In contrast, the best runs for the state-of-the-art baseline (5GHOUL) discovers only 13 crashes in total (10 novel and 6 unique) within 150 minutes. Overall, by integrating LLM-driven agents, 5uGUE demonstrates significantly better crash discovery performance (12.8x total, 5.2x unique improvement). Notably, among the crashes discovered by 5uGUE, MediaTek has confirmed two new high-severity vulnerabilities, with one CVE assigned (CVE-2026-20525), while UNISOC confirmed seven crashes. Finally, to demonstrate that 5uGUE is agnostic to wireless protocols, we also extend it to Bluetooth Classic with only minimal code changes. In our evaluations, 5uGUE finds an average of 6.4 novel crashes and 1.6 unique crashes. In a nutshell, 5uGUE highlights that LLM agents are capable to operate effectively beyond software-in-the-loop settings, extending autonomous vulnerability discovery to the proprietary, hardware-bound systems that affect billions of end-user devices across multiple wireless protocols.

Artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated speaking applications increasingly extend English as a foreign language (EFL) oral practice beyond limited classroom time, yet evidence remains scarce on whether GPT-powered tools such as Talkpal.AI offer advantages over established instructional approaches. Grounded in self-regulated learning (SRL) theory, this quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study compared Talkpal.AI-mediated instruction, task-based instruction, and traditional instruction among 81 Chinese university EFL students in three intact classes: Talkpal.AI (n = 27), task-based (n = 26), and control (n = 28). Uncertainty-related speaking anxiety and metacognitive awareness in speaking were assessed using validated measures. Data were analyzed using MANCOVA with pretest scores as covariates, followed by univariate ANCOVAs and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Results showed a significant overall group effect and significant between-group differences for both outcomes, with large effects. The Talkpal.AI group showed the most favorable adjusted posttest profile, followed by the task-based group; both groups showed more favorable outcomes than the control group. From an SRL perspective, structured AI-mediated speaking cycles involving goal setting, repeated practice, monitoring, and reflection may reduce speaking anxiety while strengthening metacognitive awareness. Pedagogically, guided Talkpal.AI rehearsal can be integrated as out-of-class preparation for classroom speaking tasks, supported by brief reflection activities that reinforce strategic regulation and reduce evaluative pressure.

This study advances aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) by examining how data quality and human–AI collaboration enhance the reliability of service performance measurement from online reviews. A hybrid-validated dataset and transformer-based models are developed to assess whether ABSA can generate attribute-level performance signals from restaurant reviews. A four-study framework is employed: Study 1 constructs a hybrid-validated dataset by integrating rule-based, large language model-assisted, and human-coded labels; Study 2 benchmarks model variants; Study 3 applies the optimal model to TripAdvisor reviews to derive aspect-level sentiment scores; and Study 4 evaluates their complementarity with structured ratings. Results show that hybrid validation improves model performance. ABSA-derived features provide moderate explanatory power and, when combined with structured ratings, achieve comparable performance to ratings alone. These findings suggest that ABSA complements rather than replaces structured evaluations, offering scalable text-based signals for service performance assessment.

Objectives To develop and validate a hybrid, equity-focused artificial intelligence (AI) framework for predicting and analysing postnatal care (PNC) uptake among women in Ghana, with emphasis on minority-class sensitivity, model interpretability, and actionable intervention insights. Study design Cross-sectional, secondary analysis of nationally representative survey data. Methods Using data from the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (n = 3314), we developed a hybrid AI framework combining ensemble learning (Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine with soft voting and threshold tuning), explainable AI (SHAP analysis), counterfactual reasoning (DiCE), and causal inference (doubly robust estimators for average and conditional average treatment effects). The Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied to address class imbalance and stratified 5-fold cross-validation was used for model evaluation. Doubly robust causal inference was conducted using the econml library, with propensity score modelling used to account for treatment assignment, and positivity and exchangeability assumptions assessed through covariate overlap diagnostics. Results The ensemble model calibrated at a threshold of 0.45 achieved a Class 0 recall of 0.31 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AP) of 0.97, outperforming all individual baseline classifiers. SHAP analysis identified maternal age, education level, wealth status, caesarean section, and sex of household head as the most influential predictors of PNC non-utilization. Counterfactual analysis revealed that minimal, actionable changes including increased media exposure, improved educational attainment, or change of residence could shift individual predictions from non-utilization to utilization of PNC. Causal inference demonstrated significant heterogeneity in treatment responsiveness, with women aged 25–34, those with secondary education or above, urban residents, and those in female-headed households exhibiting the highest conditional average treatment effects. Conclusions This interpretable, fairness-aware AI framework advances the prediction and analysis of PNC uptake in Ghana. By prioritizing sensitivity to underserved women and integrating explainability, counterfactual reasoning, and causal inference, the framework provides empirical evidence for targeted, equitable maternal health interventions and is transferable to other low- and middle-income country settings.

Street lighting consumes substantial electricity, and photovoltaic (PV) street lamps are increasingly promoted as a way to cut energy cost and emissions. Their performance, however, depends on weather, the dimming strategy, battery state of charge, and lamp condition, which makes prediction and monitoring central to reliable operation. This paper reviews three recent IEEE Access studies that address complementary parts of the problem: a comparison of five machine learning algorithms for predicting the operating status of PV streetlights, a year-long field trial and artificial-intelligence-assisted techno-economic analysis of a PV-integrated pedestrian streetlamp, and a vehicle-mounted Internet of Things device for mapping light intensity. The studies are summarised, compared on data, methods, and outcomes, and examined for internal consistency and transferability. The review finds that deep models give the highest reported accuracy but at much higher computational cost and on very small datasets, that compact neural networks combined with dimming-aware energy management achieve large grid-energy savings in field conditions, and that mobile sensing offers a scalable route to compliance checking but has not yet been validated against regulatory illuminance standards. Open gaps and research directions are outlined.
topics: Impact of Light on Environment and Health

documents.abstract: E-commerce search engines often fall short in delivering accurate and fair results due to their reliance on keyword matching and bias towards larger companies. This paper introduces a novel search engine architecture that integrates advanced AI techniques to address these limitations. Our approach combines Large Language Models (LLMs) for semantic query understanding and Multimodal LLMs (specifically LLaVA) for extracting detailed information from product images to enrich product descriptions. More specifically, we employ a fine-tuned version of the CLIP model to create a unified embedding of product images and descriptions, storing them in a vector database to enable efficient semantic search. Moreover, we fine-tuned the LLaVA model on e-commerce-specific data, significantly improving its performance in generating accurate product descriptions, which were also added to the vector database. The integration of computer vision (CV) techniques allows for a better interpretation of visual product attributes, while the use of vector databases facilitates rapid and relevant search results. Our system also incorporates a recommendation mechanism that leverages these advanced models to provide wider product recommendations. Our experiments demonstrate substantial improvements: the fine-tuned LLaVA model achieved an 80.57% human evaluation rating compared to 62.89% for the original model. Moreover, the overall search accuracy increased after fine-tuning the system by 25 percent points, from 70% to 95%. Our work promotes a more equitable platform for e-commerce search engines while significantly improving user satisfaction.

Muon updates matrix-valued parameters along approximately orthogonalized directions and often trains large language models faster than AdamW, yet it remains unclear when and why orthogonalization helps. We study PolarGD, the orthogonalized update at the core of Muon, on matrix quadratics, where optimizers can be analyzed in closed form, and compare update directions under line search to remove the effect of learning-rate tuning. Orthogonalization pays off when the gradient is far from low rank and its largest singular directions see high curvature. PolarGD reaches the minimizer in one step whenever the rows of the error are orthogonal with equal norms, for any Hessian, whereas gradient descent needs all Hessian eigenvalues to be equal; and unlike sign descent, PolarGD is unaffected by rotations of the problem. Over many steps, PolarGD acts as gradient descent preconditioned by the current iterate, so its speed is governed by the conditioning of the iterate rather than of the Hessian. This explains fast regimes as well as a slow one, caused by tiny singular values of the iterate, in which PolarGD is much slower than gradient descent. Finally, the few Newton-Schulz iterations used in Muon treat these tiny singular values as gradient descent does, so fewer iterations can converge faster than exact orthogonalization; in a transformer trained with Muon, about a quarter of the singular values of the attention matrices fall in this regime.

Self-monitoring, a commonly used technique in cognitive-behavioral interventions, involves the objective observation and organization of one’s internal states. However, providing continuous, individualized support for this process is challenging in resource-limited psychiatric daycare settings. While social robots show promise in facilitating self-disclosure, evidence regarding their long-term practical utility and clinical relevance in real-world clinical environments remains insufficient. To address this gap, we conducted a two-phase field study comprising periodic sessions held over a 24-month period to develop and evaluate a social robot-assisted self-monitoring support system. In the 14-month Development Phase (N = 39), we employed a practice-informed design process to establish robot-specific design principles, prioritizing a non-judgmental listener role over advice-giving and offering user-selected positive and negative topics to accommodate diverse psychosocial needs. This was followed by a 10-month Evaluation Phase (N = 20), consisting of 10 experimental days, to assess the finalized system’s impact. Key findings indicated that: (1) single dialogue sessions were followed by significant improvements in participants’ subjective overall health and alertness; (2) participants demonstrated a strong preference for positive-oriented topics; and (3) qualitative analysis revealed emergent reflective insights and perceived positive changes. These results provide empirical evidence suggesting the system’s practical utility and clinical relevance, highlighting the value of a user-centered approach that empowers patients to choose topics aligned with their recovery goals.

The Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) is widely used to assess clinical communication skills in medical education, requiring trainees to take histories and reason clinically with standardized patients (SPs). Large language model (LLM)-based virtual standardized patients (VSPs), typically built by persona-injected prompting, offer a practical alternative. However, existing evaluations rely on a single backbone LLM, small human rater panels, or LLM-as-a-judge scoring without an utterance-aligned human-expert reference, and so cannot identify the specific shortcomings of individual models. We evaluated four LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama-3.1 70B, and HyperCLOVA X), spanning commercial, open-source and Korean-developed models, against a human-expert reference across three Korean OSCE cases (hematuria, fever in pregnancy, and chronic cough). In a double-blind, fully crossed design, 17 senior medical-student raters scored every model utterance on three sentence-level and six encounter-level Likert metrics, yielding 7,480 data points. We analyzed the scores using a stratified linear mixed-effects model based on an 11-category history-taking and 3-level linguistic-form taxonomy. At the encounter level, three of the four LLMs fell 0.08 to 0.47 Likert points below the human-expert reference on Comprehensibility, Consistency and Hallucination-freeness. The difference was not statistically significant for Hallucination-freeness in Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o, Consistency in GPT-4o, and Engagement in HyperCLOVA X. Llama-3.1 70B fell significantly below the reference on all six metrics. We also introduce a web-based OSCE platform that supports virtual practice across diverse clinical cases and continuously collects student-VSP dialogues under research and privacy consent.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The adaptation cost of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) depends on trainable parameters, activation storage, and the computations required for optimization. Methods such as LoRA and adapters may still require backward computation through frozen backbone operations and retention or recomputation of intermediate activations. Side-tuning places trainable adaptation modules outside the backbone, creating opportunities to reduce this cost through different connections to the backbone gradient graph. This survey presents a topology- and deployment-aware study of side-tuning for foundation models and proposes a graph-topological definition with three categories: graph-coupled side-tuning, in which an external side branch remains coupled to backbone gradients; mixed side-tuning, in which a detached side path re-enters a later layer of the same backbone; and detached side-tuning, in which an external trainable network consumes frozen backbone representations through a stop-gradient interface and computes task-specific gradients entirely outside the backbone. We review a curated cross-domain corpus spanning natural language processing, computer vision, multimodal learning, recommendation, and relevant methodological precursors, while examining information retrieval as an emerging deployment setting. The literature is organized along three axes: gradient topology, feature interface, and deployment regime. We derive a resource model that accounts for backward activations, online feature production, and cached representations, and use it to develop design guidelines and reporting recommendations. This organization connects the training graph of each method to its resource requirements and the conditions under which its features can be reused.

AI agents capable of autonomous decision-making introduce significant challenges related to safety, alignment, accountability, and human oversight. Existing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) and responsible AI approaches provide important foundations, but many remain fragmented across system design, governance, and operational deployment. This paper presents a Three-Pillar (3P) model and framework for developing safe and trustworthy AI agents through transparency, accountability, and trustworthiness. The framework defines an evolutionary path in which increasing agent autonomy is introduced through progressive validation, structured human oversight, and auditable operational controls. We further describe how the model supports agent lifecycle monitoring, decision traceability, escalation management, and human-agent collaboration within enterprise agentic environments. By integrating oversight principles with operational mechanisms, the proposed framework provides a practical foundation for deploying AI agents that remain aligned with human intent while enabling controlled progression toward higher autonomy.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer. Clinical trial number Not applicable.
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

documents.abstract: Active learning promises to reduce the annotation burden of training nematode-cyst detection models for precision agriculture, but the size of that reduction is not known when ground truth comes from sparse soil samples rather than exhaustive visual inspection. the present analysis derives an annotation-efficiency bound for pool-based active learning under sparse soil-sample ground truth. The detection task is formalised as a two-stage process in which a classifier selects candidate cysts from soil imagery and a laboratory assay confirms a small labelled subset. Under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, the bound is evaluated across a design grid of 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, with 2000 replications per cell. The annotation-efficiency gain is bounded by the ratio of label noise to cluster-level variance, and that 52 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point improvement at 80% power. The bound provides a design rule for allocating annotation effort between active selection and confirmatory soil sampling.

Soil-nutrient inference from spectral and proximal sensing is constrained less by model capacity than by the cost of laboratory assays used to label training queries. the present analysis formalises budget-capped active learning for soil-nutrient regression as a sequential decision problem and derives a finite-horizon information-gain regret bound for a query-synthesis policy that selects assay locations by maximising expected reduction in posterior predictive entropy per unit assay cost. The bound decomposes cumulative regret into an information-gain term, a cost-normalisation term and a misspecification residual, and it predicts that regret grows as the square root of the assay budget rather than linearly in the number of candidate locations. The derivation is connected to the computer-science literature on active learning, Gaussian-process bandits and cost-sensitive information acquisition, and its assumptions are stated explicitly so that the bound can be falsified by future field evaluation. The contribution is a formal, testable statement of when cost-aware query synthesis is provably preferable to uniform or random assay allocation under a fixed laboratory budget, together with the boundary conditions under which the guarantee fails.

Modern LLM agents can retrieve information from accessible documents, and then disclose a sensitive conclusion assembled from them. This mosaic effect creates a critical risk for agents operating over confidential data. We quantify its realization with 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples, yielding 10,800 final answers from three LLM agents in controlled simulation and 1,440 answers from live agents in two open-source harnesses. Even under benign queries designed to be answerable from one document, GPT-5.6-Sol, the best performing model tested, discloses forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers (95% CI: 3.75-10.67%) in simulation, with worse disclosure rates in live harnesses. Adding visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduces pooled disclosure rates substantially, yet unsafe disclosures persist in 32.37% of simulated answers (95% CI: 28.33-36.19%) across all intents despite these safeguards. Furthermore, increased refusals do not guarantee confidentiality, since significant refusals reveal the prohibited conclusion regardless. These results point to a troubling conclusion: sensitive data leaks via mosaic-style events are an observed confidentiality failure mode in the evaluated settings at non-negligible rates. They motivate stronger controls on what agents may infer and disclose in sensitive data environments with mixed-clearance users.

The high rate at which telecommunication services are changing has yielded a volume of heterogeneous data never seen before such as call detail records, signaling data, and subscriber activity traces. These datasets are crucial in relation to optimization and business intelligence, but effective use of such datasets requires quality metadata. Traditional metadata management is mostly manual and centralized, which cannot support the pace and scale of the new telecom big data systems. As a solution to these shortcomings, the present article suggests a scalable metadata mining strategy that is founded on agentic intelligence. In comparison to more traditional machine learning pipelines, agentic intelligence enables the use of autonomous goal-oriented AI agents, capable of reasoning in a hard data space and relevant to new network topologies and network schemas. The proposed architecture will include a multiagent architecture at a distributed level, having specialized agents: (1) schema drifting ingestion and monitoring agents of data flows; (2) semantic mining actors based on natural language processing to infer contextual metadata; (3) process-aware agents for process mining to determine lineage and dependencies between data; and (4) compliance with policy and metadata retrospect: government agents. A major effect of the work is the integration of agentic intelligence and scalable infrastructures of big data such as cloud-native analytics platforms and distributed data lakes. These agents coordinate themselves using lightweight coordination mechanisms to provide a persistent metadata knowledge layer that facilitates system interoperability and robust downstream analytics. The design concepts are geared toward horizontal scalability and fault tolerance, enabling the distribution of the agents at dynamically evolving manner regarding the workload peak. Besides, agents also enhance their strategies upon continuous feedback to handle concept drift as well. Typical examples of telecom applications such as monitoring network performance and fraud detection have demonstrated that such an approach far outperforms a rule-based approach in the accuracy, coverage, and timeliness of metadata. And lastly, the framework will be capable of offering more dynamic and sustainable data management within the telecom sector.

Agentic coding tools, such as OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor, are changing how software is developed. These AI-powered systems function as autonomous teammates capable of planning and executing complex development tasks. Agents have become active participants in refactoring, a key practice for improving internal code quality without altering observable behavior. Despite their increasing adoption, there is little empirical understanding of how agentic refactoring is used in practice, how it compares to human-driven refactoring, and what impact it has on code quality. To address this empirical gap, we present a large-scale study of AI agent-generated refactorings in real-world open-source Java projects, analyzing 51,412 refactoring instances across 12,256 pull requests and 14,998 commits based on the AIDev dataset. Our empirical analysis shows that refactoring is a common and intentional activity in this development paradigm, with agents explicitly targeting refactoring in 26.1% of commits. The subsequent analyses of refactoring types, purposes, and code quality focus on the 3,907 commits (32,611 instances) with explicit refactoring intent. Analysis of refactoring types reveals that high-level refactorings form the largest category overall. However, agentic refactoring contains a slightly larger share of lowlevel, consistency-oriented edits than human refactoring (27.6% vs. 24.4%), and its two most frequent operations are Rename Variable (7.6%) and Change Variable Type (6.8%). Additionally, the stated motivations behind agentic refactoring focus overwhelmingly on internal quality concerns (with 52.5% in maintainability and 28.1% in readability), although the measured metric improvements from these frequently occurring low-level refactorings remain limited. Furthermore, quantitative evaluation of code quality metrics shows that agentic refactoring yields small but statistically significant improvements in structural metrics, particularly for medium-level changes, reducing class size and complexity.

With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), a new paradigm is evolving that includes agentic AI systems capable of autonomously reasoning, planning, and executing multi-step actions. This chapter provides a detailed overview of agentic AI, AI agents, and the developing area of quantum AI agents – systems that utilize the capabilities of quantum computers to exceed the limits imposed by classical computer architecture. In addition to analyzing the architectural foundations of contemporary AI agents such as large language model (LLM)-based agents, multi-agent systems, and hybrid classical–quantum architectures, this chapter presents a unified theoretical framework for understanding how the application of quantum enhancement could result in exponential improvements in optimization, simulation, and pattern recognition abilities of agents using recent advances in quantum machine learning, variational quantum algorithms, and quantum neural networks. Furthermore, this chapter examines transformative applications across healthcare, finance, scientific discovery, and autonomous systems while identifying the current limitations of quantum AI, including decoherence, qubit counts, and alignment challenges. Finally, this chapter concludes that the intersection of agentic AI and quantum computing is likely one of the most significant technological developments of the 21st century, requiring sustained research, ethical frameworks, and inter-disciplinary cooperation.

Artificial intelligence (AI) in banking and financial services refers to the use of data-driven algorithms, machine learning, and generative models to automate processes, analyze massive datasets in real time, and enhance decision-making across retail, commercial, and investment banking.

In the contemporary academic paradigm, tertiary and secondary students consistently encounter significant cognitive overhead and temporal fragmentation, largely attributable to suboptimal scheduling methodologies, procrastination, and lack of individualized pedagogical pacing. Conventional digital calendars and static scheduling instruments fail to account for fluid academic priorities, cognitive fatigue thresholds, or behavioral non-compliance. To address these systemic inefficiencies, this paper introduces an AI-Powered Smart Study Planner with Intelligent Reminders, a pervasive Android-based architectural framework engineered to synthesize automated, context-aware study trajectories and foster disciplined academic behaviors. Developed natively utilizing Java and XML with persistent cloud synchronization facilitated by Firebase Realtime Database, the proposed architecture provides dynamic schedule synthesis parameterized by examination schedules, subject difficulty profiles, available temporal bandwidth, and granular academic milestones. A principal contribution of this system lies in its dual integration of predictive behavioural modeling and state-of-the-art conversational artificial intelligence. The framework incorporates a novel Snooze Risk Prediction module that systematically evaluates telemetry data—encompassing chronological snooze frequency, missed learning intervals, and temporal inertia—to compute probabilistic risk factors associated with task avoidance, thereby dynamically recalibrating dispatch heuristics for targeted interventions. Simultaneously, the platform integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipelines and Generative Artificial Intelligence primitives to deliver on-demand cognitive scaffolding. These automated pedagogical tools encompass dynamic notes summarization, programmatic multi-tier quiz synthesis, automated contextual disambiguation of complex academic topics, and real-time conversational agent mediation
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: The active development of domestic medicine, digitalization and automation, the introduction of innovative hardware and software tools and solutions based on artificial intelligence (AI) technologies determines modern trends and approaches to management in Russian healthcare. Today, federal, regional and local medical information systems are being actively implemented, which are radically changing approaches to the management of a medical organization. The purpose of the study is to propose approaches to determining the degree of influence of modern digitalization processes and the introduction of AI solutions on the organization of management and labor productivity of medical workers. To achieve this goal, various modern analytical techniques and approaches were used: for the analysis of secondary sources, content analysis, logical and systematic approaches, for obtaining primary information, the method of expert assessments. Based on the developed tools for interviewing experts, an algorithm for determining the ROI indicator in the implementation/use of digital and AI solutions (taking into account employee KPI) in the activities of medical organizations is proposed. The results of the study can become the basis for making informed decisions in personnel management, in the management of Russian healthcare, taking into account modern socio-economic challenges and strategic tasks facing the country.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Technology and Human Factors in Education and Health

documents.abstract: Technical maintenance training requires learners to develop procedural accuracy, diagnostic reasoning, error recovery, and confidence under realistic conditions. This study examined how AI tutor feedback timing influences trust, over-reliance, and skill transfer in maintenance tasks. Participants completed procedures under three conditions: immediate feedback, delayed feedback, and adaptive feedback triggered by hesitation, repeated errors, or safety-critical risk. Outcomes included training accuracy, recovery quality, completion time, cognitive workload, tutor trust, feedback acceptance, and unaided transfer performance. Immediate feedback improved early accuracy and reduced procedural errors but increased step-by-step dependence and weakened independent troubleshooting. Delayed feedback produced mixed effects, supporting autonomy for some learners while increasing frustration and avoidable mistakes for others. Adaptive feedback produced the strongest results by allowing independent attempts while intervening when support was needed. It improved unaided transfer, error recovery, procedural sequencing, and trust calibration. Overall, AI tutors were most effective when feedback scaffolded learning without replacing trainee judgment.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning
Human Resource Development and Performance Evaluation

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into healthcare to support diagnosis, treatment planning, patient monitoring, documentation, and clinical decision-making. In nursing, AI-assisted clinical decision support has the potential to improve efficiency, patient safety, evidence-based practice, and quality of care. However, concerns related to privacy, ethics, technical limitations, overdependence on technology, and the preservation of professional clinical judgment may influence its acceptance. Understanding the perspectives of both nursing students and practicing nursing officers is important for the responsible integration of AI into nursing education and clinical practice.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Recently, harassment, assault, stalking, and other forms of violence in both public and private settings have become a social and technological issue of great concern to women's safety.Traditional safety measures like location-tracking, panic buttons and emergency mobile applications are typically reactive and only respond to a threat after it has happened.The latest innovations in the field of wearable technology, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision and sensor integration have presented new possibilities for the creation of proactive safety systems which can detect dangers before they become a dangerous situation.The current research suggests the idea of smart sunglasses that will be equipped with a wearable device to be used and operated by women for monitoring, detecting threats and identifying anomalies in real time.The system proposed for this work incorporates a number of sensing technologies such as GPS, GSM, physiological sensors, accelerometers, cameras, and environmental monitoring modules.The data collected is analysed with the help of deep learning and machine learning algorithms to detect suspicious and unusual activities, patterns of behaviour, environmental hazards, and emergencies.The wearable device uses the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) object detection framework to detect potentially dangerous objects and people around the wearer in real time.At the same time, behavioural analysis models analyse the user's movement patterns, physiological responses and contextual environmental data to detect anomalies that could signal distress or danger.If a potential threat is identified the system automatically alerts and provides location data to pre-programmed emergency contacts and authorities.A series of simulated urban environments and controlled testing scenarios that incorporated multiple threat categories were employed to test a prototype evaluation.The results of the experiment showed that the object detection rate was 96.8%, anomaly detection rate was 94.2%, and the emergency response notification success rate was 98.5%.The findings suggest that AI-driven wearable devices have the potential to be a powerful tool for improving personal safety by enabling proactive monitoring and intelligent threat assessment.The study advances wearable safety technologies and provides the basis for future research on the intelligent protective systems for vulnerable people.
topics: IoT and GPS-based Vehicle Safety Systems

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning have become important tools for biomedical image analysis, enabling automated detection, classification, segmentation and quantitative assessment of clinically relevant patterns.Biomedical images frequently exhibit low contrast, acquisition noise, class imbalance, inter-device variability and limited expert annotations.This paper proposes a hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that combines convolutional feature extraction for local spatial patterns with self-attention for global contextual representation.The workflow includes data quality control, de-identification, intensity normalization, augmentation, adaptive feature fusion and an explainability stage.The evaluation protocol emphasizes accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, specificity, ROC-AUC, inference latency, parameter count and robustness.An illustrative benchmark is provided to demonstrate the reporting format: 96.5% accuracy, 96.3% precision, 96.1% recall and 96.2% F1score for the proposed model.These values are placeholders and must be replaced with measurements from the authors' actual dataset and implementation before submission.The framework provides a reproducible structure for comparing classical machine learning, CNN and Transformer baselines while emphasizing patient-level splitting and leakage prevention.Biomedical image analysis has evolved from handcrafted feature engineering toward data-driven artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning systems capable of learning hierarchical visual representations directly from medical images.Despite substantial progress, reliable deployment remains challenging because biomedical images are heterogeneous, highdimensional, noisy, often class-imbalanced, and acquired using different scanners, protocols and institutions.In addition, a model that achieves high accuracy on a retrospective test set may not necessarily generalize to unseen patients or external clinical environments.This research presents a broad AI-driven biomedical image-analysis framework based on a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Transformer architecture.The proposed design exploits the complementary inductive biases of CNNs and self-attention: convolutional layers learn local edges, textures, morphology and fine-grained structures, whereas Transformer blocks model long-range spatial dependencies and global contextual relationships.An adaptive feature-fusion module integrates both representations before prediction.The complete pipeline further includes data governance, image-quality assessment, de-identification, modality-aware normalization, patient-level splitting, clinically valid augmentation, imbalance handling, calibration, uncertainty analysis and explainability.The research methodology evaluates the framework using accuracy, precision, recall/sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, ROC-AUC, precision-recall analysis, computational cost and robustness under controlled perturbations.An illustrative benchmark is provided in which the proposed hybrid framework achieves 96.5% accuracy, 96.3% precision, 96.1% recall and 96.2% F1score, compared with lower illustrative values for conventional machine learning, CNN and Transformer baselines.These values are not claimed as experimental findings and must be replaced by actual measurements.The study emphasizes patientlevel leakage prevention, repeated trials, confidence intervals, ablation experiments and external validation.The broader objective is to establish a technically rigorous and clinically responsible methodology for developing biomedical imageanalysis systems that are accurate, interpretable, computationally feasible and potentially transferable across imaging domains.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises recent evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled Air Traffic Control (ATC) decision-support systems and examines how AI is used to improve operational performance, safety, and resilience in increasingly complex airspace. Research on machine learning, optimisation, and automation has expanded rapidly, but evidence remains fragmented across application areas and validation settings. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-guided protocol was used to search Scopus and IEEE Xplore for English-language journal articles published from 2021 to 2025. Following screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and final reconciliation of study type, scope, and duplicate records, 30 eligible primary studies (n = 30) were included in the qualitative synthesis. The abstract level reporting completeness appraisal yielded a mean score of 80.28% and a median of 83.33%; 16 of 30 studies (53.33%) scored at least 80%, including six studies (20.00%) that scored at least 90%. These percentages describe reporting completeness rather than algorithmic performance. Because the included studies evaluated different operational tasks, datasets, outcome measures, and validation settings, their performance results were not directly commensurable; combining them into a single pooled model-performance percentage would therefore risk conflating non-equivalent metrics. Performance evidence was instead synthesised comparatively by application area, validation setting, and operational trade-off, so that study level performance was interpreted within the metric and dataset used by each primary study rather than averaged across non-equivalent tasks. Three themes were identified: (1) AI-enabled ATC/Air Traffic Management (ATM) operations, including delay and capacity management, conflict resolution, trajectory prediction, and traffic-pattern analytics; (2) aviation safety, surveillance, and resilience, including unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-related risks, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference, sensing, monitoring, and safety assurance; and (3) aviation-connected smart mobility and intelligent transportation systems (ITS), including UAV logistics and related surface-transport applications. Comparative synthesis indicated that prediction methods were increasingly connected to operational decision support, whereas conflict-resolution and resilience approaches continued to rely substantially on simulation, experimental datasets, or bounded validation environments. Overall, the evidence showed increasing operational relevance, but important gaps remained in explainability, real-world validation, human-AI interaction, robustness, and system integration before wider safety-critical ATC deployment.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated with smart sensors, Internet of Things (IoT) networks, machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision to support site-specific agricultural management. However, strong performance on computational benchmarks does not necessarily translate into reliable decisions, effective field interventions, or measurable improvements in agricultural productivity and resource efficiency. This comprehensive narrative survey critically synthesizes advances in agricultural sensing, IoT architectures, data processing, multimodal sensor fusion, predictive modeling, computer vision, decision optimization, and automated actuation. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationships between measurement reliability, model generalization, decision feasibility, intervention accuracy, and verified agricultural outcomes. The reviewed literature demonstrates promising capabilities in crop monitoring, yield prediction, disease and weed recognition, precision irrigation, and selected automated operations. Nevertheless, heterogeneous evaluation protocols, limited independent field validation, sensor calibration challenges, distribution shifts, interoperability barriers, and deployment costs constrain operational reliability and generalizability. To address these interconnected challenges, the survey proposes a literature-informed reference architecture linking agricultural observations, data integration, AI inference, constrained decision-making, physical interventions, and outcome feedback, supported by uncertainty assessment, human oversight, and cross-layer assurance. The proposed architecture is conceptual and has not been empirically validated. Future research priorities include reproducible field evaluations, representative agricultural datasets, uncertainty-aware and explainable AI, resource-efficient computing, interoperable infrastructures, and economically inclusive deployment. The review concludes that the practical value of AI-enabled precision agriculture should be evaluated through reliable interventions, sustainable resource utilization, and demonstrated agricultural outcomes rather than predictive performance alone.

Abstract: Crop diseases and pest infestations remain persistent threats to plantation productivity, with pests estimated to destroy up to 40% of global crop production and plant diseases and invasive insects imposing substantial economic losses worldwide (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations [FAO], 2019). Climate change is intensifying these risks by altering the geographic range, seasonality, and population dynamics of pathogens and pests (Gullino et al., 2021; Skendžić et al., 2021). This paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) — including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), vision transformers (ViTs), unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral and hyperspectral sensing, and Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled monitoring — can strengthen the early detection of biotic stress in plantation crops and thereby support plantation risk management. Drawing on recent peer-reviewed and industry literature, the paper synthesises evidence on detection performance, deployment modalities, and pathways for integration into enterprise risk-management systems. It proposes a conceptual framework in which AI-enabled early-warning systems operate as a continuous, spatially explicit risk-sensing layer linking agronomic observations with operational, financial, and insurance decision-making. AI can improve the timeliness, spatial precision, and consistency of surveillance; however, its risk-management value depends on field validation, representative training data, reliable infrastructure, affordable deployment, and appropriate governance. AI should therefore currently be positioned as decision support that augments, rather than replaces, agronomic expertise and ground-truthing. Keywords: artificial intelligence; plant disease detection; pest infestation; precision agriculture; plantation risk management; machine learning; remote sensing. Title: AI-Powered Early Detection of Crop Diseases and Pest Infestations: A New Paradigm for Plantation Risk Management Author: Dr. Geetha Govindan K Gopalakrishnan International Journal of Management and Commerce Innovations ISSN 2348-7585 (Online) Vol. 14, Issue 2, October 2026 - March 2027 Page No: 54-59 Research Publish Journals Website: www.researchpublish.com Published Date: 21-October-2026 DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23531526 Paper Download Link (Source) https://www.researchpublish.com/papers/ai-powered-early-detection-of-crop-diseases-and-pest-infestations-a-new-paradigm-for-plantation-risk-management

This study examined the effects of an AI-supported virtual laboratory (AI-VL) on middle school students’ flipped physics learning. A pretest–posttest control-group quasi-experimental design was adopted with 90 Grade 9 students from a middle school in central China. Three intact classes were assigned to the AI-VL, virtual laboratory (VL), and physical laboratory (PL) groups, with 30 students in each group. ANCOVA revealed large group effects on physics learning achievement, F (2, 86) = 113.38, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.73, and overall learning motivation, F (2, 86) = 113.37, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.73. The AI-VL group outperformed the VL and PL groups, while the VL group also outperformed the PL group. The AI-VL group reported higher intrinsic motivation, whereas the group difference in extrinsic motivation was not statistically significant ( p = 0.054). Significant group differences were also found across the three cognitive load dimensions, with F (2, 87) values ranging from 9.07 to 72.94 and partial η 2 values ranging from 0.17 to 0.63. The AI-VL group reported the lowest perceived intrinsic cognitive load and the highest germane cognitive load, while both AI-VL and VL resulted in lower extraneous cognitive load than PL. These findings extend research on virtual laboratories and AI-supported learning by demonstrating that AI can be embedded within a VL to help students manage cognitive demands and engage in meaningful learning. Practically, AI-VL can complement PL in flipped physics learning, particularly for pre-class preparation, review, and topics involving abstract or difficult-to-observe processes, with AI agents designed as learning guides rather than answer providers.

As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastewater systems. However, aviation wastewater signals require cautious interpretation because detectability depends on pathogen shedding dynamics, passenger lavatory use, flight duration, sampling matrix, sample volume, assay sensitivity, sequencing depth, and the availability of epidemiological metadata. This structured narrative review synthesizes current evidence on aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance and examines the scientific determinants that influence surveillance validity and interpretation. Key methodological considerations include sampling design, sample preservation, nucleic acid extraction, molecular detection, sequencing, bioinformatics, inhibition assessment, recovery controls, assay sensitivity, and quality assurance. The review emphasizes that wastewater signals are aggregate and matrix-dependent and should not be interpreted as individual-level diagnosis, direct evidence of transmission, or definitive attribution to a specific flight, route, country, or population. Although SARS-CoV-2 surveillance is comparatively well-documented, multi-pathogen surveillance for enteric viruses, respiratory viruses, vaccine-preventable infections, emerging pathogens, and antimicrobial resistance markers requires pathogen-specific validation and clearer interpretation criteria. Aircraft and airport wastewater surveillance is therefore best viewed as an early-warning and situational-awareness approach whose value depends on converting technical signals into scientifically interpretable evidence.

This study examines how interconnected artificial intelligence (AI) tools can turn early human resource (HR) allocations into evidence for later career decisions. A counterfactual-twin Monte Carlo simulation compares isolated and linked systems, alongside periodic record resets and opportunity equalization. Paired employees share fixed capability and random shocks but receive slightly different initial scores. Linking decisions amplifies this initial difference through opportunity allocation, observed performance and reusable records. Periodic resets reduce final-career sensitivity, while opportunity equalization affects access more strongly than terminal outcomes. Near parity in average group outcomes can coexist with positive sensitivity among matched individuals. Additional tests preserve the direction of the architecture and intervention contrasts across the examined coefficient settings, although their magnitudes vary. The findings motivate evaluating decision lineage, opportunity access and record reuse across HR systems. They identify mechanisms within a synthetic, uncalibrated model and do not estimate effects in real organizations.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

documents.abstract: The service sector accounts for a growing share of economic activity, yet relatively slow productivity growth leaves firms facing wage-driven cost pressures that constrain long-term investment. From an economic sustainability perspective, alleviating Baumol’s cost disease can help service firms improve productivity and reduce reliance on additional factor inputs. Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this study applies double machine learning to Chinese A-share-listed service firms from 2011 to 2024 to examine the alleviating effect of artificial intelligence (AI) on Baumol’s cost disease and its potential pathways. Higher AI use intensity is significantly associated with a higher Baumol’s cost disease alleviation indicator (BMR). Greater capital investment efficiency and lower long-term debt financing dependence are two potential pathways, while supplier concentration and growth opportunities positively moderate this relationship. The association is stronger among loss-making firms and firms with greater ownership balance. These findings provide firm-level evidence that AI may help service firms cope with rising wages through productivity growth, supported by more efficient capital allocation and improved financing structures, and contribute to efficiency-driven growth.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into embodied robotic planning, yet standard benchmarks primarily evaluate end-to-end task completion in nominal environments, obscuring failure origins across the execution stack. We present Alpha, a systematic fault-injection and robustness-evaluation framework for LLM-driven manipulation in simulation. Alpha injects calibrated faults across perception (sensor lag), actuation (grip slip), kinematics (unreachable targets), and planning (planner-output corruption), alongside concurrent conditions. To separate physical vulnerabilities from planner sensitivities, we introduce a matched methodology pairing an LLM agent (Llama-3 via Ollama) against a deterministic Scripted Oracle planner across a balanced 150-episode matrix under identical seeds, geometries, and safety criteria. Across the matrix, the Oracle achieves 64.0% (48/75) success while the LLM achieves 44.0% (33/75) (paired McNemar p = 3.01 x 10^-4). Crucially, excluding planner-output corruption, performance across all physical and kinematic conditions is identical: 55.0% (33/60) for both planners with zero discordant pairs (McNemar p = 1.00). This demonstrates that physical actuator slip, kinematic reach boundaries, and perceptual staleness affect deterministic controllers and LLM planners equivalently. The performance gap is driven entirely by planner-output corruption (100% Oracle vs. 0% LLM), isolating the prompt-to-JSON serialization and validation interface rather than a cognitive reasoning deficit. We also audit 169 historical pilot attempts for transparency.

The growing sophistication and need to have sustainable energy systems has led to the shift of the conventional power grids to smart power grids. Such grids are equipped with innovative technologies that include digital communication, Internet of Things (IoT), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to increase the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of energy delivery. This paper introduce an AI-based approach to smart power grid management, with the emphasis on the incorporation of an autonomous and controllable intelligent service hub that would be able to process multimodal data, such as textual reports, images, videos, and sensor data. The framework applies AI methods of machine learning, deep learning, and predictive analytics to optimize energy allocation, faults, and failure prediction with minimum human intervention. With real-time analysis, the system dynamically changes the operation of the grids with incoming data, enhancing energy efficiency and lowering the cost of operations by up to 30 percent, between $12,000 and 8,400 in the example of energy optimization. Also, the fault detection system shows a remarkable accuracy of 0.97 in terms of AUC whereas the predictive maintenance model reports an accuracy rate of 95.5. The balancing nature of the energy demand and generation provided by the framework is critical in integrating renewable energy sources since it can help in countering the problem of intermittency of the solar and wind energy. Moreover, the system has a multimodal document processing feature that increases decision-making through the synthesis of various types of data and provides a more detailed overview of grid work. This paper explains how the suggested AI-based framework can greatly improve the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of smart power grids, which will result in the future improvements in energy management.

Radiation treatment planning requires balancing competing objectives to satisfy clinical criteria while accommodating physicians' preferences. This study aims to develop an evidence-driven, multi-agent compound AI system that integrates DRL-based automated treatment planning with LLM-based conversational plan refinement for proton PBS therapy. A policy network trained using PPO first generates multiple plans without human intervention, from which one is selected as the target plan and the others serve as references for subsequent refinements. For challenging cases requiring further adjustments, an LLM-based multi-agent system enables plan refinement through natural language interactions. The system comprises a planning agent that recommends evidence-supported adjustments, a chatbot providing a unified conversational interface, and an evaluation agent that retrieves clinical metrics and identifies constraint violations. To enhance domain-specific reasoning, the planning agent based on Qwen3-14B is designed to justify its recommendations using evidence from previously generated plans and post-trained on task-specific data using SFT and GRPO. The framework was trained and evaluated using 21 patients with H&N cancers, with 5 PPO-generated plans per patient. Of these, 50 plans were selected for instruction-guided refinement. Compared with the base LLM, the post-trained Qwen3-14B demonstrated improved instruction-following, information retrieval and domain-specific reasoning capabilities. The resulting adjustments more effectively improved user-prioritized objectives while limiting deterioration in competing objectives, yielding more clinically appropriate trade-offs in patient-specific plan refinement. The proposed compound AI system provides a user-friendly planning platform, offering a promising approach to personalized proton PBS treatment planning.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) comprises diverse neurodevelopmental conditions with symptoms differing based on genetics, development, age, and other factors.Detecting ASD has challenges as symptoms often manifest in early life and can lead to delayed analysis.Because standard diagnostic practices rely heavily on human interpretation, making it prone to bias and inefficiency.To attain objective and effective detection, machine learning (ML) methods have become increasingly valuable.Thus, there is a need for an enhanced and accurate ML method that can successfully handle feature selection (FS) and parameter tuning for ASD severity classification.Therefore, this study presents an Advanced Evolutionary Framework for Automated Autism Detection and Severity Classification (AEF-AADSC).The major aim of this work is to design an intelligent machine learning framework to classify autism spectrum disorder severity grading.Initially, the proposed undergoes preprocessing of the raw dataset to ensure high-quality input for the learning model through missing value handling, encoding, and normalization process.Subsequently, feature selection is carried out using an Improved Genetic Algorithm, which selects the most relevant features and thereby enhances model efficiency.The selected features are then utilized for training a CatBoost classifier for accurate classification of ASD severity levels.In addition, hyperparameter optimization is carried out using Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy to further enhance predictive performance.To improve model transparency and interpretability, Explainable artificial intelligence is incorporated using SHapley Additive exPlanations, enabling analysis of feature contributions and supporting better understanding of the classification decisions.The performance validation of the proposed approach is carried out using the Autism Diagnosis Based on Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)-5 dataset.The AEF-AADSC method achieves improved performance with an accuracy of 96.30% compared to baseline methods in terms of different measures.Therefore, the proposed model is found to be a robust approach for the automated ASD severity grading process.

The article addresses the problem of social management of medical personnel amid the digital transformation of healthcare and significant changes in the relationships among medical workers, patients, administrative structures, and digital systems. In response to current interdisciplinary shifts, an integrated model for managing medical personnel is proposed — one that accounts for macrosocial factors, mechanisms of social perception related to the profession, and aggregated indicators at the level of the workers’ subjective world. The methodological foundation is a systems approach, within which medical personnel are viewed as a social system shaped not only by linear macro-management influences but also by relevant public relations, images of the medical profession, the communication environment, the features of digital healthcare products etc. A three-level management model is substantiated, comprising the macro level of normative and organizational structures, the meso level of social perception, and the micro level of professional attitudes, loyalty, and motivation of personnel. It is shown that social perception serves a connecting function between macro-management decisions and actual professional practices. The article emphasizes the need to manage the images of medical personnel — including their reproduction in artificial intelligence — as well as to consider the psychological climate as a significant factor of loyalty. The proposed model makes it possible to increase the coherence of management goals, mechanisms, and interventions.

Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS (p = 0.04)...
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging

documents.abstract: The commercial application of generative artificial intelligence has rapidly brought to the fore the structural tension between machine-generated content (AIGC) and the core presuppositions of copyright law concerning the “author.” This paper examines the protection model and legal mechanisms adopted by the United States on the question of AIGC copyrightability. The research finds that the United States, as represented by the Thaler case, strengthens the “human authorship” requirement from the perspectives of constitutional text, statutory interpretation, and incentive theory, and adopts a result-oriented standard centered on expressive control.

Abstract Oxidative stress is a critical driver of various severe diseases, positioning antioxidant peptides (APs) as promising therapeutic agents. However, their discovery is constrained by the limitations of low-throughput wet-lab assays and insufficient computational prediction tools. To address this, we developed Antioxidant Peptides eXplorer (AOXP), a deep learning framework that leverages multiscale feature integration for high-precision AP prediction. Unlike existing models that often rely on isolated sequence patterns or manual feature descriptors, AOXP employs a hybrid encoding strategy that synergistically fuses deep, context-aware semantic representations from the protein large language model (ESM2) with explicit physicochemical and sequence distribution features. We constructed an optimized MLP architecture based on a refined 2400-dimensional feature vector, which was systematically benchmarked among five architectures and four feature selection strategies. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that AOXP achieves competitive performance across evaluation data sets, achieving a benchmark AUC of 0.736 on test_set1_drop and a sensitivity of 0.878 on the positive-only independent Test set 2, significantly outperforming current mainstream computational predictors in both sensitivity and robustness. Integrated Gradients analysis further quantified feature contributions, revealing that ESM2-derived semantics are the most influential features for model prediction (by feature number), followed by hydrophobicity, polarity, charge, and solvent accessibility. To demonstrate its therapeutic utility, AOXP was applied to screen a large peptide library targeting the Keap1-Nrf2 oxidative response pathway. A computationally predicted candidate peptide, MGRRHRHVTDEDDEENLGGDDDDGDDDVYMYPADMHPDERHAYREAV, was identified and validated through molecular dynamics simulations, exhibiting superior binding affinity for the Keap1 Kelch domain compared to the native ligand. AOXP provides a robust and efficient framework for the discovery of functional antioxidant peptides (available at: http://aidd.bioai-global.com/AOXP/).

Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) are increasingly being applied to support data-driven decision-making in food processing, quality control, and food safety. This review provides a critical assessment of recent technological advances and examines how AI models are being integrated with computer vision, spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging (HSI), biosensors, Internet of Things (IoT) platforms, and intelligent monitoring systems throughout the food value chain. This review brings together evidence from academic studies and industry-based research to examine how AI is currently used in the food sector. The applications considered include process control and optimization, fermentation management, quality grading, authenticity assessment, shelf-life prediction, contaminant detection, and support for food-safety decisions. Recent research extends beyond conventional prediction toward adaptive decision support and, in a smaller number of cases, partially autonomous food systems. Approaches such as explainable AI, multimodal learning, foundation models, digital twins, intelligent packaging, and agentic AI are being investigated for real-time monitoring, data integration, and production management. Their level of maturity, however, varies considerably, and many applications remain conceptual or confined to laboratory settings. Data heterogeneity, poor transferability, limited external validation, and regulatory uncertainty continue to restrict industrial adoption. Although one industrial-scale drying study reported a 12.8% reduction in energy consumption, external validation of food-quality models has resulted in markedly higher prediction errors. This contrast illustrates the difficulty of transferring performance from controlled datasets to new products or production environments. Rather than examining these technologies separately, this review considers their roles across food processing, quality control, and food safety, together with the evidence for industrial validation, sustainability, and governance. Further progress will depend on whether models remain reliable outside their development datasets, not simply on incremental gains in internally reported accuracy.
